text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Banks are aggressively promoting mortgages at interest rates of around eight percent. Mortgage rates should drop if Portugal joins the euro.
- The liberalisation of Portuguese telecommunications will encourage investments in infrastructure totalling 200 billion escudos in the next two years, according to a government forecast.
- Shareholders of ship repairer Lisnave meet today to approve the launch of a human resources company, Gestave - Recursos Humanos, under a reorganisation programme for the group.

- In 1992 the Professional Training Institute granted a six-year loan for 90.5 million escudos to the CGTP trade union umbrella group for the refurbishment of a building, but the CGTP has not repaid the loan.
- Portuguese trade deficit worsened by 7.6 percent in 1996, according to the National Statistics Institute. Exports of car parts fell, but other export sectors improved.
- The main source of new jobs from the second half of 1998 will be the environment sector, overtaking the civil construction sector, a government study says.
- Representatives of the World Jewish Congress will meet officials from the Bank of Portugal tomorrow in order to discuss the probe into Portuguese purchases of Nazi gold.
